\chapter{Protocols: declared thresholds and controls}\label{t3ann:protocoles}

\begin{origine}
\textbf{At the start}, the method of Volumes~I and II: each measurement has its control, and every new control must be able to fail; a threshold derives from a named quantity and is declared before the measurement, by a dated commit; a cost is judged in ABBA series; every figure one depends on is redone by a second path; a refuted sentence is struck through.
\textbf{This appendix establishes}, for Volume~III, the list of declared thresholds with the quantity from which each derives and its verdict; the table, generated from git, of each threshold file and of the time of the commit that created it; the controls and their breaks; the amendments made before reading, and those made after, stated as such; the protocols of the judges.
\textbf{What remains} is what git cannot prove: that no exploratory reading preceded a threshold (\cref{t3ann:sec:faux-a}).
Sources: the threshold files of \cref{t3ann:tab:seuils-dates}, the deliverables and the judgements of the chapters, \fichier{memoire/tome3/JUGEMENT-figures3.md} (§ 4.4), \fichier{memoire/outils/tome3_cassures.py}.
\end{origine}

\section{What is inherited}\label{t3ann:sec:herite}

The rules do not change from one volume to the next; they are set out in Volume~I (appendix on the protocols) and applied to the program in Volume~II (its appendix A). Volume~III practises them more densely, because the quest for the genome declared, from 16 to 27 October 2026, thirty-five files of thresholds, criteria and amendments (\cref{t3ann:tab:seuils-dates}), often by agents working at the same time: the rule ``the threshold is declared before the pass, and the time of the commit is authoritative'' is the only one there that allows the order of events to be read. Three forms recur, which the volume names the same way everywhere:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{success and death}: a mechanism has a success threshold and a death threshold; between the two, it is ``inconclusive'' or ``open'', and says so (the triage of mimicry declares them this way for its six leads);
\item \textbf{the rule of paired differences}: a variant $b$ is better than a variant $a$ if $\bar d + 2\sigma < 0$, $d = \mathrm{KL}_b - \mathrm{KL}_a$ position by position, $\sigma$ the standard deviation by windows; equal if $\lvert \bar d\rvert \le 2\sigma$; worse otherwise (rule of lot R, Volume~II; \cref{t3jug:sec:sigma} for the reason for $\sigma$ by windows);
\item \textbf{the announced gain}: a median speed ratio is announced only if it exceeds $1 + 2\sigma$, $\sigma$ the relative noise of a file against itself in the same session; the judge of the construction tightened the rule to $\sigma = \max$ over the files of the session (\cref{t3jug:sec:plan}).
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{The guards of the figures.} The data tools of the figures (\fichier{memoire/outils/tome3_*.py}) stop at their first guard; the judge of the third pass of the figures forced nine of them to false by its own means, in a copy, and all of them stopped their script (\fichier{memoire/tome3/JUGEMENT-figures3.md}, § 4.4): GN2 (III-8.5, a rate of the real codec changed), GN1 (III-10.1, 767 experts decoded instead of 768), G7 (III-9.6, the frame rule), J5 and J6 (III-8.6 bis), the companion (III-8.6 bis), $j = 11$ (the row of III-9.1), E1 (III-9.7), the second spike (III-7.4, where it is the compilation that stops) and DN7 (III-4.8). \fichier{memoire/outils/tome3_cassures.py} replays four of these breaks; it has no place in a build, since it forces the guards to false.

\section{The amendments}\label{t3ann:sec:amendements}

A threshold may change: before the reading, with its reason and its time; after, never without saying so. The volume counts three kinds.

\paragraph{Before the reading, because the instrument could not answer.} The spectra lead amended its main verdict on 21 October (§ 4 bis of \fichier{genome/pistes/spectres/seuil.md}, commit \texttt{bfc1c8c}), before any reading of the real spectra: a trial of the instrument on 40 draws of true Paretos ($n = \num{2880}$, $\alpha = 2.5$ and $3.5$) had returned all of them ``not settled'' against the log-normal. The criterion had no power; the lead's judge has since shown that it is impossible to satisfy at any size (\cref{t3spe:ch}). The main verdict is reported as declared, next to the amended verdict.

\paragraph{Before the measurement, because an earlier measurement called for it.} Lot B declared the rule for settling the two $\lambda$ at 12:15 on 17 October, after B0 and before the $\lambda = 0$ coding (\cref{t3sno:sec:b2}), then the calm rules of session s2 on the 21st at 23:59, before any pass. P1 declared its post hoc analyses before computing them (\fichier{genome/mimetisme/P1/posthoc-declare.md}); P2 its selective demotion, a post hoc hypothesis stated as such, before opening the 20b (\fichier{seuil-declare-selectif.md}); P4 an amendment to the reading of the protocol, before any launch; P5 three addenda, each before its launch; P6 amendment A1, before any simulation (\cref{t3mim:ch}).

\paragraph{After a reading, stated as such.} Two controls of lot B were corrected after the pass that had made them fall without cause: the substitution counter (``768'' become ``substituted = read'') and the tolerance of the recomputed KL ($10^{-12}$ absolute become $10^{-9}$ relative). Neither decides a verdict; both are struck through in place, with the time (\cref{t3sno:sec:protocole}). The margin-weighted criterion of P3 was declared after the reading of $N = 146$ and before any new pass, which its file says in its title.

\section{The protocols of the judges}\label{t3ann:sec:juges}

Each step of the volume had its judge, who had built nothing of what it judged. Their protocol is the same everywhere:
\begin{enumerate}
\item declare its thresholds before any measurement, with a prediction (the judge of the construction: ``equal'' for B2, $\times 1.38$ for $r(R/B)$; both refuted, and published as such);
\item redo each published figure by a path of its own (another decoder, another KL, another text, another experimental design), without reading the judged code before having written its own;
\item by default, \emph{a figure not reproduced does not hold}; a figure reproduced but wrongly attributed is struck through as an attribution and kept as a measurement;
\item read the deliverable sentence by sentence against its logs, and classify what does not hold into serious findings (which change what the project would do next) and minor ones;
\item carry the strike-throughs into the judged deliverable, without removing anything, and write its own ``What could be wrong'' section.
\end{enumerate}
A judge's judgement can itself fall: that of the construction attributed the gap of the disk stage to ``the physical state of the files''; the judge of the disk placement overturned it on 27 October, and the judgement carries the correction at every place (reserve R1, \cref{t3jug:sec:r1}).

\section{What could be wrong}\label{t3ann:sec:faux-a}

\begin{faux}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Git dates a commit, not a reading.} That the threshold is committed before the first log does not prove that no exploratory reading preceded it; the judge of the tropical lead says so of its own lead (the 222 lines of code committed 74 seconds after the threshold were written before it; writing a reader is not reading).
\item \textbf{The times written in the notes} do not always agree with git, by a few minutes; the time of the commit is authoritative.
\item \textbf{The table of criteria is a selection}: it keeps those that decide a verdict of the volume; the threshold files contain others (second-rank controls, reading criteria without a verdict), which can be read in the files of \cref{t3ann:tab:seuils-dates}.
\item \textbf{The verdicts of mimicry} are those of the judges of each lead, reported by \cref{t3mim:ch}; the second draw of P3, in progress elsewhere, may change its own.
\item \textbf{The dated table} sees only the files whose name says ``seuil'', ``critère'' or ``déclaré'' (\emph{threshold}, \emph{criterion}, \emph{declared}); a threshold written in another file (a specification, a deliverable) escapes it.
\end{itemize}
\end{faux}
